Allelically overdispersed tiles (data-driven allelic mask)

Source: R/caller.R
allelic_noisy_tiles.Rd

Per tile of class size, the method-of-moments beta-binomial overdispersion of the null rows' allele votes, rho = (sum (nA - n/2)^2 - sum n/4) / sum n (n - 1) / 4, then z_rho = (log rho - median) / MAD of log rho over the tiles with at least min_votes votes per null row. Tiles with z_rho > k_mad are masked: a local stretch whose votes are far more overdispersed than the genome (e.g. a 5 Mb tile with rho 0.040 vs a genome median of 0.011 over 5 Mb tiles) and that inflates the chromosome-level allelic LLRs of the cells. The votes of the atoms in masked tiles (atoms_in_tiles()) are then left out of the allele features (update_allelic_features(), call_scn(params$mask_allelic = TRUE)).

Usage

allelic_noisy_tiles(
  feat_long,
  null = NULL,
  size = "5Mb",
  k_mad = params$mask_rho_mad,
  min_votes = params$mask_min_votes,
  params = caller_defaults(),
  f0_mad = params$mask_f0_mad,
  f0_min = params$mask_f0_min,
  rules = "rho"
)

Arguments

feat_long

features long table (class, region, chrom, nA, n_hap) with a null definition

null

optional logical null flag per row

size

tile class

k_mad

threshold in MADs of log rho (params$mask_rho_mad)

min_votes

minimal mean votes per null row of a tile for it to be assessed (params$mask_min_votes)

params

caller_defaults()

f0_mad

bias threshold in MADs of d0 (params$mask_f0_mad)

f0_min

minimal deviation d0 of a bias outlier (params$mask_f0_min)

rules

the rules that define masked: any of "rho", "f0"

Value

data.table tile, chrom, start, end, n_rows, votes, rho, z_rho, assessed, masked, f0, d0, z_f0, masked_rho, masked_f0 (one row per tile)

Details

Shared allelic bias (params$mask_f0): per tile also the vote-weighted haplotype fraction of the null rows f0 = sum nA / sum n_hap, its deviation d0 = |f0 - 0.5| and z_f0 = (d0 - median) / MAD of d0 over the assessed tiles. A tile is a bias outlier (masked_f0) when it is assessed, z_f0 > f0_mad and d0 > f0_min: a stretch whose allele fraction is off 1:1 in the null cells for reasons that are not somatic copy number (germline CNV or segmental duplication, imprinted or allele-specific accessible regions, mapping bias, false heterozygous SNPs), against which the 1:1 allele null of every cell is wrong. The rule sees only the null rows, but it cannot tell such a shared bias from a real clonal event whose carriers remain among the null cells: an event frequent enough for that looks the same and can be masked (in a simulation with a focal event in 35 % of cells, 60 of 96 carriers stayed in the null set and all four event tiles were masked). The mask is a diagnostic to be read with the list of masked tiles, not a filter to apply blindly to samples that may carry clonal events. |f0 - 0.5| covers two orientations of the allele features: under loo (block) orientation the fraction is major-oriented (a biased tile sits above 0.5), under chromosome-anchored orientation it sits at f0 or 1 - f0. Under mirrored orientation each block counts its major allele, so f0 is above 0.5 in every tile by an amount set by the votes per block: the statistic measures coverage, not shared bias, and call_scn() does not apply the bias rule (it says so in the run notes and warns). allelic_bias_tiles() gives the same table over all cells before calling.

rules selects which flags make up masked (the tiles whose atoms are dropped): "rho" (the default and the behaviour of earlier versions: masked = masked_rho), "f0", or both (union).
